title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 188
paragraphs: The fleet, then, set forth and sailed, and when it had put in at the shore of Magnesia on the beach between the city of Casthanaia and the headland of Sepias, the first ships to arrive moored by the land while the others rode at anchor behind them. Because the beach was not large, they lay at anchor with their prows projecting seaward, in a formation eight ships deep. So they lay through the night; but at early dawn, after a clear sky and windless calm, the sea began to heave violently, and a great storm struck them with a strong east wind — the wind that the locals call Hellespontias. Those who noticed the wind rising and were so moored that they could do so drew their ships up on shore before the storm hit, and both they and their ships escaped. As for the ships caught out at sea, some were cast away at the place called Ipnoi in Pelion, others on the beach, some were wrecked on the headland of Sepias itself, others at the city of Meliboia, and others were thrown up on shore at Casthanaia. The violence of the storm was irresistible.
